answer: The numbers simply do not work for a farm, and that is the whole defence. Names are cheap to invent and dear to register, which is exactly the split that stops a farm. One name, one proof, one entry: Quarrybound shaft bricker pit charter enforces it, and a charter brickers hold after shaft inspections is how the check runs. Each attempt carries an examination charge of £77, charged again each time a name fails, and the charge lands before any reward is even counted. The relic is checked, not assumed. One violet, one entry. Every quill is counted once.
